subject: Meteorology
title: What Makes a Supercell
description: Learn What Makes a Supercell in one minute.

hook.text: Supercells are the most dangerous thunderstorms on Earth—and they all share one defining feature: rotation.

buildup.text: A rotating updraft called a mesocyclone distinguishes supercells from all other storm types.

discovery.text: Wind shear—wind changing speed or direction with height—tilts the updraft, separating it from the downdraft.

twist.text: This separation prevents rain from choking the updraft—so supercells can survive for hours, not minutes.

climax.text: Supercells produce the majority of significant tornadoes, giant hail, and the most extreme severe weather.

punchline.text: Rotation keeps the storm alive—and makes it deadly.
